clue.text: Official notes that woman's review courses

parts.note: a ref, short for referee, is a sports official
re is the second note of the sol-fa scale, so two or more are res
the possessive pronoun for a woman

explanation.surface: A referee writes comments on a colleague's performance at training sessions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Official notes' reads as one phrase about paperwork, but the official and the notes are separate pieces: REF + RES + HERS.
explanation.definitionFit: Refreshers are short courses that bring someone's earlier training up to date, a kind of review.

clue.text: Carouse, as opening of formal dance postponed

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter, which is the one that gets moved
something postponed is put off until later, so the leading letter goes to the end

parts.note: a prom is a formal school dance in the US

explanation.surface: Partygoers keep on drinking while the start of the ball is delayed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Opening of' points at the first letter of the dance, and 'postponed' sends it to the back: PROM becomes ROMP.
explanation.definitionFit: To romp is to frolic boisterously, close to carousing or partying noisily.

clue.text: Pasta, chopped up? Cut it fine

indicators.note: chopping something up breaks it into bits that can be put back together in another order

parts.note: the three words supply nine letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A cook slicing pasta is told to make the pieces small.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut it fine' sounds like a cooking instruction or an idiom about leaving little margin; it is the letter supply. Fettucini is a variant spelling of fettuccine.
explanation.definitionFit: Fettucini is a flat ribbon noodle, a type of Italian pasta.

clue.text: Spooky Eastern lake

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for east or eastern
Lake Erie is one of the Great Lakes

explanation.surface: A haunted body of water somewhere in the east.
explanation.definitionFit: Eerie is a synonym for spooky: strange in a frightening way.

clue.text: Toss nitrogen in the sky

parts.note: to heave is to throw something heavy
N is the chemical symbol for nitrogen

explanation.surface: Someone throws nitrogen up into the air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like it places the nitrogen inside something, but it only joins wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Heaven, often plural, is a literary word for the sky or firmament overhead.

clue.text: In conversation, interpreted "planting device" as a kind of tree

indicators.note: in conversation words are heard rather than seen, so their sound is what counts

parts.note: the past tense of read, which is said the same way as the colour
a seeder is a machine that sows seed, and it is said like the conifer

explanation.surface: Someone mistakenly took a piece of farm equipment to mean a tree.
explanation.definitionFit: The red cedar is a North American conifer, a species of tree prized for its timber.

clue.text: Mostly high, cold, soft mineral

indicators.note: mostly means not all of it, so the final letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: high and tall are synonyms
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on a tap

explanation.surface: A list of a rock's qualities: lofty, chilly and yielding.
explanation.walkthrough: The commas make it a list of adjectives, but 'high' and 'cold' are pieces and 'soft mineral' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Talc is the softest mineral on the Mohs hardness scale, used to make talcum powder.

clue.text: Commercial nearly put down Dwight's opponent

indicators.note: nearly means not quite all, so the last letter of the word is cut off

parts.note: an ad is a commercial
laid is the past tense of lay, to put down

explanation.surface: A political advertisement that almost demolished a presidential candidate.
explanation.walkthrough: Dwight is Dwight Eisenhower, who beat Adlai Stevenson in the 1952 and 1956 US presidential elections.
explanation.definitionFit: Adlai Stevenson was the Democratic candidate who ran against Eisenhower twice, so his first name identifies him.

clue.text: Gallop slowly and hide where you'd find a 14

parts.note: a canter is a horse's gait slower than a gallop
to bury something is to hide it

explanation.surface: A rider eases the horse's pace and goes into hiding.
explanation.walkthrough: 14 is ARCHBISHOP, and the Archbishop of Canterbury heads the Church of England, based in Canterbury, a cathedral city in Kent.
explanation.definitionFit: Canterbury is the English city that is the seat of the senior archbishop of the Anglican Church.

clue.text: Tom or Sam, swapping $100 for a dollar, gets loose

indicators.note: swapping one thing for another means one letter is taken out and a different word put in its place

parts.note: Uncle Tom and Uncle Sam are both famous uncles
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, slang for a hundred dollars
a buck is slang for a dollar

explanation.surface: An uncle exchanges a hundred-dollar bill for a single dollar and is let go.
explanation.walkthrough: The C in UNCLE is the one swapped out, and BUCK goes into its place.
explanation.definitionFit: To loose is to unfasten or set free, which is what undoing a buckle does.

clue.text: Rita is one or 28, unfortunately

indicators.note: something that has gone unfortunately has gone wrong, so the letters of the cross-referenced answer are put in disorder

parts.note: the answer to 28 across, the aboriginal creation era

explanation.surface: A woman named Rita is described as either one thing or, sadly, another.
explanation.walkthrough: Lovely Rita is the Beatles song about a meter maid, a woman who issues parking tickets. Its letters and 28's are the same nine.
explanation.definitionFit: Rita in the Beatles song is a traffic warden who writes parking tickets, an example of a meter maid.

clue.text: Material for hose that's only coiled neatly at first

indicators.note: a coiled hose is twisted round on itself, so the letters are wound into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

indicators.note: at first points to the opening letter of the word just before it

parts.note: the first letter of neatly

explanation.surface: A garden hose that is only tidily wound up at the start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hose' suggests a garden hose, but here it means stockings, which are made of this fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: Nylon is the synthetic fibre from which women's stockings, called hose, are made.

clue.text: Evangelist's clue, using a phonetic anagram

indicators.note: a phonetic rearrangement shuffles the spoken sounds rather than the written letters, so the word must be said aloud

parts.note: the word clue is said k-l-oo; reorder those three sounds as l-oo-k

explanation.surface: A gospel writer leaves a hint that can be solved by rearranging it.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue says outright what to do: take the sounds of the word clue, not its letters, and put them in a new order.
explanation.definitionFit: Luke is one of the four evangelists, the traditional authors of the gospels.

clue.text: Suit relating to the death penalty?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a business suit is slang for a company boss
second meaning, a playful one: something to do with executions

explanation.surface: A lawsuit about capital punishment.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the second sense is a pun: the word really relates to carrying things out, as in the executive branch, not to execution of prisoners.
explanation.definitionFit: An executive is a company manager, called a suit in slang, and the word looks as if it derives from execution.

clue.text: Prelate is attracted to both sexes in saucy business

indicators.note: in places one word inside the others, between the two halves of the phrase that follows

parts.note: arch means cheekily knowing or saucy
a shop is a business
bi is short for bisexual

explanation.surface: A senior churchman turns out to be bisexual and caught up in a racy enterprise.
explanation.walkthrough: The racy surface hides a sober answer: the 'saucy business' splits into two words with BI between them.
explanation.definitionFit: An archbishop is a bishop of the highest rank, a senior prelate or church dignitary.

clue.text: Has power with $1,000 in checks

indicators.note: in means the money is placed inside the word that follows

parts.note: to rein in is to hold back, so reins are checks or restraints
G, for grand, is slang for a thousand dollars

explanation.surface: A wealthy person holds sway thanks to a large sum paid by cheque.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Checks' looks like bank cheques to go with the dollars, but it means restraints.
explanation.definitionFit: A monarch who reigns holds royal power, so reigns means has power or rules.

clue.text: Reformed cons hail saint

indicators.note: something reformed has been made over into a new shape, so the letters are recast

parts.note: the two words supply the eight letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Prisoners who have gone straight praise a holy figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reformed cons' reads as a phrase about ex-prisoners, but 'Reformed' acts on both words.
explanation.definitionFit: Nicholas is the name of a saint, the bishop of Myra behind the legend of Santa Claus.

clue.text: Betray bats

parts.note: surface reading: a command to inform on flying mammals, or on the people who wield cricket or baseball bats; setter's reading: the word bats is what you get when you write the word stab from its end to its start

explanation.surface: An instruction to sell out some bats.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer split in two describes the second word: stab, back to front, spells bats. The first word is a plain definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To backstab is to betray someone who trusts you, attacking them behind their back.

clue.text: Barber keeps up with seven holding leadership in Rome: Julius Caesar, Mark Antony, et al.

definitions.text: Julius Caesar, Mark Antony, et al.

indicators.note: keeps means holds within, so the barber's word goes round the next piece

parts.note: to trim hair is what a barber does
U is used as a short form of up

indicators.note: holding means wrapping around, so the number goes round the next piece

parts.note: VII is seven in Roman numerals

indicators.note: leadership means the head, the first letter of the place named

parts.note: the first letter of Rome

explanation.surface: A Roman barber gives seven leading men their haircuts.
explanation.walkthrough: Both containers sit side by side, each wrapping one letter. Caesar sat in the First Triumvirate and Antony in the Second.
explanation.definitionFit: Triumviri is the Latin plural of triumvir, each of three men sharing power in a Roman triumvirate.

clue.text: In a manner that's idiotic and irrational, with sexy, well-built exterior

indicators.note: an exterior is an outside, so one word forms the outer shell around the other

parts.note: studly is slang for attractive and muscular, like a stud
pi is the best-known irrational number

explanation.surface: Someone foolish and illogical who nonetheless has a hunky outside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Irrational' looks like part of the definition alongside 'idiotic', but it is the famous irrational number.
explanation.definitionFit: Stupidly is the adverb of stupid, meaning done in a foolish or senseless way.

clue.text: Styles primitive dwellings, adopting air conditioning to start

indicators.note: adopting means taking in, so the dwellings take the following letters inside

parts.note: huts are simple, primitive shelters
taken as written

indicators.note: to start points to the opening letter of the word just before it

parts.note: the first letter of conditioning

explanation.surface: Someone fashions basic shacks and fits them with air conditioning first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Air conditioning' reads as one appliance, but only the C of the second word is used, with AIR whole.
explanation.definitionFit: Haircuts are the styles in which hair is cut, so styles works as a plural noun for them.

clue.text: One who might be 17, or 21, or older and unacceptably nosier

definitions.text: One who might be 17, or 21, or older

indicators.note: something done unacceptably is done wrongly, so the letters of the word are disordered

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An older person grows nosier in a way others can't accept.
explanation.walkthrough: 17 and 21 are ages here, not cross-references: a high-school senior is around 17, a college senior around 21, and a senior citizen is older still.
explanation.definitionFit: Senior names a final-year student in US high school or college, or an elderly person.

clue.text: Gleaming penny beneath front half of Olympic sled

indicators.note: the front half keeps only the leading two of four letters, dropping the back half
in a down answer, a piece beneath another is written after it

parts.note: the luge is a small sled raced at the Winter Olympics
a cent is the US penny

explanation.surface: A shiny coin lies under the nose of an Olympic sled.
explanation.walkthrough: The penny is read first but sits second, because 'beneath' in a down answer means after.
explanation.definitionFit: Lucent is a literary word for shining or giving off light, a synonym of gleaming.

clue.text: Urchin with the first answer, down in Mexico: "You are spontaneous"

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous child or urchin
the answer to 1 down
tú is Spanish for you

explanation.surface: A street child speaking Spanish tells someone they are impulsive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Down in Mexico' sounds like a place, but 'down' belongs to the cross-reference: the first down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Something impromptu is done without preparation, on the spur of the moment, so spontaneous.

clue.text: Criticize and train a group of experts, perhaps

parts.note: to pan is to criticize harshly, as a reviewer does
the El is an elevated railway train, as in Chicago

explanation.surface: Instructions to criticize and then coach a team of specialists.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Train' looks like a verb to go with criticize, but it is the noun: an elevated railway.
explanation.definitionFit: A panel is a small body of specialists convened to judge or discuss, so a group of experts is one example.

clue.text: Duck, Duck, Goose, for instance!

parts.note: surface reading: the playground pastime in which children sit in a circle and one runs round tapping heads; setter's reading: three wildfowl that hunters shoot for sport and the table

explanation.walkthrough: The name of the playground pastime is also a list of three wildfowl, and one word covers both the pastime and the hunted birds.
explanation.definitionFit: Duck, Duck, Goose is a children's game, and ducks and geese are game, wild birds hunted for food.

clue.text: Retrospective covering 2001, for example — that's an easy one

indicators.note: retrospective means looking back, so the result is read from end to start
covering means wrapping round, so the abbreviation goes outside the year

parts.note: e.g. is the abbreviation for for example
MMI is 2001 in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A film retrospective including 2001: A Space Odyssey, an easy choice.
explanation.walkthrough: '2001' looks like the Kubrick film, but it is just the year in Roman numerals.
explanation.definitionFit: A gimme is slang for something easy, like a short putt in golf that is conceded.

clue.text: Wilder means of inheritance

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the actor who played Willy Wonka, known by his first name
second meaning: the unit of heredity in DNA

explanation.walkthrough: 'Wilder' looks like the comparative of wild, but it is the surname of the comic actor of Young Frankenstein.
explanation.definitionFit: Gene Wilder was the American comic actor, and a gene is the biological unit passed from parent to child.

clue.text: Accord, possibly, with sweetheart and lawyer

parts.note: hon, short for honey, is a term for a sweetheart
a DA is a district attorney, a US prosecuting lawyer

explanation.surface: An agreement reached with a lover and an attorney.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Accord' looks like an agreement, but it is the car model; 'possibly' marks it as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: The Accord is a car model made by Honda, so the maker is what such a car is.

clue.text: 10 cataclysmic days during which the world was created, according to aboriginal mythology

definitions.text: days during which the world was created, according to aboriginal mythology

indicators.note: a cataclysm is an upheaval, so the letters of the referenced answer are thrown into a new order

parts.note: the answer to 10 across, a parking-ticket officer

explanation.surface: Ten days of upheaval in which, as Australian myth has it, everything began.
explanation.walkthrough: '10 cataclysmic days' reads as a count of days, but 10 is a cross-reference whose letters are reworked.
explanation.definitionFit: The Dreamtime, or Dreaming, is the era of creation in Australian Aboriginal belief, when ancestral beings shaped the land.

clue.text: Deftly conceal a tree

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to hide a card or coin in the hand, as a conjuror does
second meaning: a tropical tree with a crown of large leaves

explanation.walkthrough: The surface asks for hiding a tree, but the two halves are separate meanings: a conjuror's sleight of hand and a tropical tree.
explanation.definitionFit: To palm something is a magician's trick of hiding it in the hand, and a palm is also a tropical tree.

clue.text: In return, New York's got the magnitude to put things together

indicators.note: in return means turned back, so the abbreviation that follows is read from end to start

parts.note: NY is the abbreviation for New York, plus the S of the possessive
taken as written
size and magnitude are synonyms

explanation.surface: New York has the scale needed to assemble things, in exchange for something.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe-S is part of the letters, not just grammar.
explanation.definitionFit: To synthesize is to combine separate elements into a whole, which is putting things together.
